transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

E011 on Bosch ovens is most commonly associated with a control key being detected as held down, which fits the beeping and the controls being locked out. Some references also associate it with temperature feedback, so I cannot confirm that alternative from the code alone—but the unusable, beeping control panel makes a stuck button or control-panel fault the leading possibility. 1. Turn the oven off at its cooker isolator switch or consumer-unit breaker for five minutes. Do not remove any covers. Restore power and see whether E011 comes straight back. A one-off electronics glitch may clear; an immediate return points to a persistent fault.
2. With the oven isolated, press each front-panel button once, gently but firmly. Check for one that feels jammed, remains depressed, is sticky from residue, or does not click like the others. Wipe the fascia only with a barely damp cloth, then dry it—do not spray cleaner into the controls. If E011 returns immediately and no button is obviously stuck, the usual repair is diagnosis/replacement of the control panel or its control electronics by an appliance engineer. Don’t keep trying to run the oven while it is beeping and locked out.

Did the power off for 5 mins at the cooker switch and dried the panel with a towel first (there was still some spray residue along the bottom edge). It's come back up normally, no code, and it heated to 180C fine. Anything else I should do?

The spray residue along the lower edge of the panel may have briefly made a key appear to be held, triggering E011; the successful reset and normal heating to 180°C are reassuring. For future cleaning, spray cleaner onto a cloth rather than directly onto the fascia, wipe gently, and keep liquid away from the bottom edge, buttons and display. A lightly damp cloth followed by a dry one is best. No further action is needed unless E011 returns. If it does recur when the panel is dry and clean, or a button becomes sticky/unresponsive, stop using the oven and arrange an engineer to assess the control panel/control electronics.

candidates: Stuck or continuously pressed control button / control panel fault (high)

reading.symptom: displaying E011, beeping and controls unusable

tags.checkGiven: Check the cooker switch (the large switch on the wall near the oven) is on, and look at the fuse box to see whether a breaker for the cooker

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model HBS534BS0B; code E011.
The fault they reported is: "displaying E011, beeping and controls unusable". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Temporary moisture/cleaner residue affecting the control panel (high)
plan: They asked: "Anything else I should do?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: Dried the control panel with a towel: The oven came back normally with no error code.
Heated the oven to 180C: It heated to 180C fine.
